title: Big O Notation Quiz Generation
content:
# What is the primary purpose of Big O notation in computer science?
- To measure the exact execution time of an algorithm in seconds across different machines
- To count the exact number of assembly instructions generated by a compiler
-* To describe the asymptotic upper bound of an algorithm's running time or space requirements
- To determine the exact amount of RAM consumed in megabytes during runtime
## Option 3 is correct because Big O notation is used to classify algorithms according to how their running time or space requirements grow as the input size grows, focusing on the asymptotic upper bound while dropping constants and lower-order terms.

# Which of the following represents logarithmic time complexity?
- O(N)
-* O(log N)
- O(N^2)
- O(2^N)
## Option 2 is correct because O(log N) denotes logarithmic time complexity, commonly found in algorithms that divide the problem space in half with each step, such as binary search.

### Explain why drop-in constants and lower-order terms are omitted when expressing the Big O complexity of an algorithm.

# What is the Big O time complexity of accessing an element in an array by its index?
-* O(1)
- O(N)
- O(log N)
- O(N log N)
## Option 1 is correct because arrays allow random access via memory addresses, meaning retrieving an element by index takes constant time regardless of the array's size.

### Given a nested loop where the outer loop runs N times and the inner loop runs N times, what is the overall time complexity and why?

# Which growth rate outpaces all others in the standard hierarchy of Big O complexities?
- O(N^2)
- O(N log N)
-* O(2^N)
- O(N)
## Option 3 is correct because exponential time complexity, such as O(2^N), grows much faster than polynomial, linear, or logarithmic complexities as the input size N increases.

### What does space complexity measure in the context of Big O notation, and how does it differ from time complexity?

# What is the worst-case time complexity of standard Binary Search on a sorted array of size N?
- O(N)
- O(N^2)
-* O(log N)
- O(1)
## Option 3 is correct because Binary Search halves the search space in each iteration, resulting in a logarithmic worst-case time complexity of O(log N).

### Describe what Big O notation represents when we talk about the "worst-case" scenario versus the "average-case" scenario.
